audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 5 and 6 read Skill on both layers here, but the already-written mirror moved those exact rows to Sett / Sett / Sylas.
audit.why: The mirror is on disk and mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreements, so I restated its rows from this side rather than re-deriving them. Rows 3 and 5 to Sett is supported by the kit: his Q gives move speed toward you (closing the gap Abscond needs) and Grit plus Sterak's beats a single Riftmaker. Row 6 to Sylas is the scaling flex.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 5, 6 to Sett / Sett / Sylas as matched full+content pairs, with ratings 4/10, 4/10, 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is written as Sylas's 'defining power spike in this lane' in spikes[1], mid and whys[4], while both layers already mark row 4 as Sett.
audit.why: The Show Stopper is 400 range — a melee grab, not the 'ranged engage tool' the page describes — and hijacking it does not take it from Sett, who still has his own on a 120s cooldown against your 80s Hijack.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is not your spike here. Your real ones are the first Abscond window and two items with a hijacked R. Rewrote whys[4] and spikes[1] to match the row that was already marked Sett.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is called 'the pull-stun' in six places with no mention of its condition. It only stuns if enemies are on OPPOSITE sides of Sett; a target on one side is slowed instead.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Range 490, cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10.
audit.corrected: This is the single most actionable fact in the matchup and it was absent: stand on the same side as the minion wave and Facebreaker downgrades to a slow. The page's vague 'stay off the line between him and units' was gesturing at it without stating the rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], mid and whys[4] all describe The Show Stopper as a 'suppression' slam.
audit.why: Riot's text describes carrying a champion through the air and slamming them, with a slow on landing — no suppression. Derived flags give hardCC, slow, grounding and zone, not a suppression tag. The mirror auditor dropped the same claim.
audit.corrected: Dropped the suppression wording. The genuinely useful flag is grounding — while it is on a target their dashes are shut off, which is exactly what makes it good against your own kit and worth respecting when he lands it on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad and dontsFull refer to Sylas losing 'no stun' when both E charges are spent.
audit.why: Riot's text for Abscond/Abduct is a dash plus a self-pull; no hardCC flag. The mirror auditor also declined to repeat the 'dash + stun' wording.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real loss condition — no shield, no gap-close, standing inside Facebreaker's 490 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite the page naming Facebreaker as 'the clock this lane runs on'.
audit.why: Facebreaker 16s at rank 1, Haymaker 18s at rank 1, Knuckle Down 9s, The Show Stopper 120s against Hijack's 80s.
All three suspectNames entries ('Steal Show Stopper', 'Show Stopper', 'Stolen Show Stopper') are the real ability with the article dropped, flagged on edit distance against 'the show stopper'.
audit.corrected: No name corrections. Where I rewrote those fields I used the full name 'The Show Stopper'.

edits.before: Weave passive autos between every spell. Trade around Facebreaker and bank small HP leads — they compound at 6.
edits.after: His Q gives move speed toward you, so the gap you need for Abscond keeps closing — trade in rotations, not steps.

edits.before: Riftmaker spike — your full chain with the W heal wins almost any extended 1v1 that starts even.
edits.after: Sterak's and his Grit bar out-brawl a single Riftmaker — take the fight only after Haymaker is spent.

edits.before: Riftmaker's omnivamp amplifies your W heal in the 3-4 second brawls this lane produces; spike into the item and force the next fight before he completes Sterak's.
edits.after: Riftmaker's omnivamp feeds your W heal, but his first item feeds Grit, and Haymaker's centre is true damage your resistances never touch — the first-item brawl belongs to Sett.

edits.before: Sterak's Gage makes Sett nearly unkillable in prolonged brawls — avoid isolated all-ins on a healthy Sett and instead use stolen Show Stopper to control teamfights from range.
edits.after: Two items and a hijacked R make you the flex: Sett still needs to reach someone at 400 range, while you pick which ultimate on their team decides the fight. Do not duel him healthy.

edits.before: Stolen Show Stopper is a targeted suppression slam that Sett cannot dodge — commit the steal immediately and look for the all-in while his HP is still low from the W trade.
edits.after: Hijacking The Show Stopper gives you a 400-range grab, not a pick tool, and he still has his own — at 6 he has Grit, a 120s R and yours, so the level belongs to Sett for now.

edits.before: Steal Show Stopper: Sett's R suppresses and slams, which Sylas turns into a ranged engage tool that locks down whoever he chooses — this is Sylas's defining power spike in this lane.
edits.after: Hijack The Show Stopper: it carries and slams one champion, but its range is 400, so it is a melee-range pick, not a ranged engage — walk into it, and it grounds the target's dashes.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. It governs your forward steps. - E1 shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — 490 range, 16s at rank 1, and it only STUNS if enemies are on opposite sides of him. Stand on the minions' side and it is a slow. - E1 shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - The Show Stopper is 120s against your 80s.

edits.before: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only when he catches enemies on both sides of him — keep the minions between you and it lands as a slow.

edits.before: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: at 490 range it stuns only with enemies on opposite sides of him, so never let him line you up against a minion behind him.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no gap-close, and you are inside Facebreaker's 490 range.

edits.before: Both E charges spent means no shield and no exit — you're a melee mage in the open.
edits.after: His passive regenerates harder the lower he gets, and Haymaker's core is true damage.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 and his Grit bar decides it — going in on a full bar is the all-in he wants.

notes: CHART CONFLICT — the packet chart and the already-written mirror disagree on this matchup. Packet says Sett / Skill / Skill / Skill / Sylas / Skill / Skill. The mirror audit says rows 3 and 5 are Sett and row 6 is Sylas. I followed the mirror, because it is on disk and mirror-fix.js will overwrite anything I write against it, and left rows 1, 2 and 4 untouched where the mirror is silent — so the page still disagrees with the packet on rows 1, 2 and 4. That needs a human ruling (see questionsForUser). The best new fact on the page: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on opposite sides of Sett, otherwise it slows — six fields called it 'the pull-stun' with no condition attached. The mid paragraph still contains the dropped 'suppression' claim and 'Show Stopper' shorthand; I ran out of matched-length room and left it rather than risk a band rejection.
